subject: Dedicated capacity proposal: QoS guarantees, throughput & commit terms
messages:
From: Sasha Green <sasha@veridianhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing & contract questions

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our infra team asked me to start the sizing and commercial discussion for a dedicated GPU pool to serve our chat and summarization features. High-level workload:~6M generation tokens / month, median request payload ~1.8k tokens, p95 context length ~6k tokens (we chunk longer docs), peak concurrent requests ~220 during US business hours.

Key asks from procurement and infra:
- What GPU pool size would you recommend to meet p95 latency < 350ms for generative chat at peak concurrency?
- Can you provide a pricing table for reserved commits (12-month vs 24-month) and associated discounts?
- Do you offer throughput guarantees or credits for missed SLOs? If so, how are they defined?
- Any constraints on model size or quantization that would affect quality?

We also need to understand how autoscaling/bursting would interact with reserved capacity and whether hybrid (reserved + burst) pricing is possible.

Can you send a short proposal and the typical SLA/credits language so procurement can review? We prefer a single PDF with workload assumptions called out.

Thanks,
Sasha
Sasha Green
Head of Product Ops — Veridian Health

Attachments: workload_samples.csv (sample request logs)
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sasha Green <sasha@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing & contract questions

Hi Sasha — really helpful details, thanks. A couple clarifying Qs before we draft a proposal:

1) 6M tokens/month — is that counting both prompt + completion tokens? If you have a sample P95/median split we can model cost more accurately.
2) For the p95 latency target, is that measured from client-side request to first token or to end-of-stream? We typically size to first-token for interactive chat.
3) When you say peak concurrent 220, is that sustained for multiple hours (e.g., 3–6 hours), or is it short spikes (minutes)?
4) Any requirement around on-prem VPC isolation or is hosted Dedicated acceptable?

We’ll put together two options: (A) conservative baseline pool sized to meet p95 <350ms at 220 concurrency for your current model profile; (B) an optimized pool that uses model quantization + smarter KV prefix caching for lower cost but with a small quality delta we’ll quantify.

I’ve looped in Ben for the pricing/commit tiers and Jordan for throughput/SLO language. We should have a draft proposal + redlines ready by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing & contract questions

Folks — I ran a quick throughput model against Veridian's provided sample logs (thanks Sasha). Summary and recommended commercial structure below.

Sizing assumptions (conservative):
- Workload: 6M tokens/month (prompt+completion)
- Median request: 1.8k tokens; p95 context length: 6k tokens
- Peak sustained concurrency: 220 for ~4 hours/day during business days
- Target p95 latency: first-token < 350ms for the production transformer (causal) model

Recommended GPU pool configuration (baseline):
- Pool: 8x A100-80GB equivalent workers (NVIDIA A100-ish throughput profile per worker)
- Effective concurrent capacity: ~28 concurrently-served long-sequence chats with KV caching enabled; we offset this with an inference service tier using a multi-worker request fanout (per-request sharding) to support 220 concurrent short-to-mid length requests. Practically this maps to 8 workers + autoscale burst policy.
- Autoscale burst: +4 on-demand workers (same HW) available to spike up to ~160 additional concurrent short requests for up to 30 mins/session.

Performance guarantees and credits:
- SLO: p95 first-token latency < 350ms measured at Redwood edge for production model variant.
- If monthly SLO attainment < 99.5%, customer receives credits equal to 5% of that month's reserved commit fees for each 0.5% shortfall, capped at 50%. (We can redline language per legal.)

Commit / pricing (list rates are illustrative; final numbers in attached PDF):
- 12-month reserved commit: base $XX,XXX/month for the 8-worker pool; 10% standard commit discount.
- 24-month reserved commit: base $XX,XXX/month; 18% discount + 1-month credit on signing.
- Hybrid option: 70% reserved capacity + pay-as-you-go burst (on-demand) at a blended lower on-demand rate (we propose 60% of list on-demand for burst when you have a reserved commit).

Discount negotiation levers:
- Higher commit levels (>= 12 workers equivalent) unlock additional tiered discounts (up to 25%).
- Multi-year: additional ~4–8% for 36-months with annual payment commitment.
- Usage floors and clearly defined workload profiles reduce risk and improve pricing (we ask for a trimmed 3-month historical sample to lock rate bands).

Attachments included: dedicated_pricing_proposal_v3.pdf (proposal + sample SLA), workload_profile_summary.csv (derived Qs/medians), redline_commit_terms.docx (initial legal).

Jordan — can you confirm the exact phrasing we want in the SLO credits section? Also, Mina, I included a note on model quantization impact in the PDF — call it out if we want a separate low-cost configuration.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Sasha Green <sasha@veridianhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@veridianhealth.com
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — initial sizing & contract questions

Thanks Ben — this is exactly what procurement needed to start redlines. A few quick items: 

- The hybrid 70/30 reserved/burst is attractive. Can you send a worked example showing monthly expected spend at our 6M tokens profile for both 12m and 24m commits? A simple table is fine.
- We will want stronger uptime credit language for mission-critical workflows. Our legal will suggest 1% credit increments starting at 99.0% — can you share precedent?
- Please send the DocuSign for the 12-month baseline so procurement can route internally; we’ll attach our internal PO number.

If you can get the DocuSign + worked example over by EOD today, we’ll aim to circulate to legal and get back with redlines by Thursday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sasha
